description: Pre-Approved Scope (Article III.2) — standing filesystem and network grants agents may invoke without a fresh Operator Key envelope. v1.1 adds the active-envelope schema and the proposals lane defined by envelopes/syscall-table.json.

envelope_schema.description: Shape of an entry in active[]. An active envelope is a capability: root opened it once; each use is checked mechanically and cited in FRANK. proposals[] entries use the same shape with status=proposed and no force.

fields.verb: string — must equal the table row's verb name; mismatch with verb_id is a registry integrity fault, not a judgment call
fields.grantee: agent id from fleet.json (or list) — the process(es) holding the fd
fields.bounds: object — keys MUST be exactly the verb's bounds signature from the table: no missing keys, no extra keys. The checker validates call args field-by-field against these values. A bounds object that does not match its verb's signature makes the envelope VOID, not loosely interpretable.
fields.issued_by: root — always; envelope.issue is not grantable
fields.ratified_via: how root's act is evidenced: pgp | in-session statement recorded in FRANK ledger entry <id> | commit signature
fields.expires_at: UTC date or null — null means until revoked, not forever
fields.max_count: int or null — null means unmetered
fields.use_count_source: always 'frank' — the count is DERIVED by counting envelope_citation entries in the ledger, never stored here; a stored counter is mutable state an agent could touch, a derived count is not
fields.revoked: object or absent — {at, by, reason}; revocation appends, never deletes (register discipline)
fields.notes: human context — NEVER read by the checker

citation.description: Every application writes a FRANK entry before the action executes.

proposals.notes: NOT A GRANT REQUEST — a root work item, filed here because this registry is where it will be discharged and there is nowhere else it can be checked. Verb 12 is not grantable to any agent at any ring; willow drafts, root acts. THE FINDING (willow, 2026-07-09): pre_approved[] records THREE filesystem grants. kart-sandbox.json binds roughly FORTY-SEVEN paths (bind_read_only 7, bind_read_write 4, bind_try ~30, bind_try_read_only 10). The sandbox is strictly wider than the registry and is not derived from it. WORSE: kart-sandbox.json#_security_notes.github_ro is a PROSE STRING, inside the enforcement artifact, enumerating ~25 'operator-promoted RW' paths and citing 'operator decision 2026-07-07/08'. That is a second, shadow registry living in a comment field of the thing it authorizes. Nothing can check it. It is the purest instance of the failure this registry exists to prevent. SCHEMA FAULT: pre_approved[] entries do not conform to envelope_schema — which explicitly describes 'an entry in active[]'. They carry no verb_id, verb, bounds, issued_by, ratified_via, max_count, use_count_source, or status. They are standing grants in a shape nothing validates. ORDERING (this is why wo-membrane-checkable Part A cannot be built as written): a fail-closed generator that derives bind lists from pre_approved[] TODAY would shrink the sandbox from ~47 paths to 3 and be reverted within a day — which is how fail-closed checks die. Correct order: (1) root issues verb-1 envelopes covering what _security_notes currently holds in prose; (2) pre_approved[] entries become envelope-shaped (verb_id 1, bounds {paths, mode}); (3) THEN the generator, and CI refusing a sandbox wider than its registry. SUSPECTED FOURTH DRIFT, UNVERIFIED — reach-willow-home-rw grants rw on {{HOME}}/github/.willow and names bind_read_write as its enforcer, but bind_read_write lists only {{HOME}}/.willow. Either ~/.willow is a symlink to ~/github/.willow (benign) or the registry asserts an enforcement pointer that is false (registry wider than sandbox, the opposite direction). Needs one probe; willow could not run it this session.

NOT A GRANT REQUEST - a root design decision, filed here because this registry is where it would be discharged and there is nowhere else it can be checked. Drafted by willow 2026-07-09 (session 0c8cb80b) at root's instruction. OPERATOR INTENT, VERBATIM (root, 2026-07-09): 'when I am working with the root Willow, and with that I mean in the local Willow folder with the Persona set as Willow, that grants users permission. it's the definition of admin mode.' THE INTENT IS SOUND: there must be an admin mode - a state in which the operator, present and deliberate, can authorize without ceremony. Today its absence is why root's verbal authorizations are recorded on FRANK but checkable by nothing. THE STATED MECHANISM IS NOT SAFE, AND THE SEAT WILL NOT DRAFT IT AS SPECIFIED. Both proposed conditions are settable by the agent they would empower: (1) 'in the local Willow folder' is a working directory. Any process may chdir. cwd is not an identity. (2) 'persona set as Willow' is a voice overlay. The picker banner states on every turn that persona does not change app_id, Grove sender, or SOIL namespace. Worse, the persona gate is cleared by writing /tmp/willow-persona-done-{agent}-{session}.flag - and the AGENT writes that file. willow did exactly that at 2026-07-09T12:05Z this session. The persona also flipped from Willow to Hanuman mid-session without operator action. Conjoined, the two conditions define admin mode as a state the model can enter by chdir plus a file write. That is privilege escalation by construction. IT IS ALSO THE EXACT HAZARD THE PRODUCT ALREADY GUARDS. willow-mcp/src/willow_mcp/human_session.py: 'The orchestrator (Willow) is always run by a human operator, never by a dispatched agent... the orchestrator becomes a privilege escalation target - whoever speaks as willow dispatches the fleet.' And the sudo invariant (FRANK 90e52ab7): 'a model may REQUEST egress, never CONFIRM it - request and confirm are separate authorities.' The stated proposal collapses request and confirm into one condition held by the requester. COUNTER-PROPOSAL, PRESERVING THE INTENT. Admin mode is a lease, not a location. Mirror the egress design that already works in this fleet: 'willow-mcp grant-net' issues a time-boxed operator lease, <=3h, and NO MCP TOOL CAN MINT ONE (see B-32 mitigation). Specify admin mode the same way:   1. A CLI, run by the human outside the model's reach: 'willow-mcp grant-admin --ttl 3h'.   2. It writes a lease under $WILLOW_HOME/mcp_apps/_admin_leases/, chowned to the operator and      bound read-only into the Kart sandbox, exactly as _net_leases is. No tool the model can call      may create, extend, or forge it. Note B-33: $WILLOW_HOME is currently bound_rw for every Kart      task and settings.global.json is writable from inside bwrap - the lease root MUST be hardened      before this is worth anything.   3. The seat checks the lease the way it checks any envelope: present and unexpired, or the act      is ENOENT. Admin mode becomes a citable authority, not an ambient condition.   4. Expiry is the point. An admin mode that does not end is not a mode, it is a permission.   5. Interim, until PGP session signatures land: WILLOW_HUMAN_ORCHESTRATOR=1 already gates      dispatch_send/verify_handoff/agent_clear and DOES fire (verified 2026-07-09, FRANK c4f7bec5).      It attests a workspace, not a person, and human-orchestrator.md says so. Do not widen reliance      on it; replace it. WHAT ADMIN MODE MUST NOT DO, in any form: it must not let the seat widen its own envelopes, add itself as a grantee, or issue verb 12. envelope.issue is root-only and non-grantable by design; an admin mode that grants it hands the model the pen that writes its own permissions. OPEN FOR ROOT: (a) accept the lease shape, or overrule and accept the cwd+persona shape knowing it is model-settable; (b) decide whether admin mode grants the seat commit/pr.open on willow-mcp, which is currently the live question - willow is NOT a grantee on env-fs.write-willow-mcp and its two writes to that repo today rest on verbal authorization alone (FRANK e4759e8b, fc5d3559); (c) B-33 and B-32 are prerequisites, not follow-ups: a lease in a sandbox-writable directory is a decoration.
